method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from CareSearch, Flinders University (funded by the Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing) 'Dyspnoea — Clinical Evidence Summary' (updated 13 April 2026), 16 claims; LICENCE: © CareSearch, Flinders University — 'No Information authored by or on behalf of us may be copied, modified or reproduced in any way without our written permission.' (read at https://www.caresearch.com.au/about-us/contact/terms-and-conditions/). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from European Society for Medical Oncology, ESMO Guidelines Committee (Hui D, Maddocks M, Johnson MJ, Ekström M, Simon ST, Ogliari AC, Booth S, Ripamonti CI), ESMO Open 5(6):e001038, doi 10.1136/esmoopen-2020-001038 'Management of breathlessness in patients with cancer: ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines' (published 10 December 2020), 18 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC7733213). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. The ranked international source (ERS 2024 clinical practice guideline on symptom management for adults with serious respiratory illness) returned a Cloudflare bot challenge (HTTP 403) at publications.ersnet.org and is not in PMC, so it was not used. This Australian evidence summary was used instead. Edition 2.0 adds S2, the ESMO 2020 Clinical Practice Guideline, a graded society guideline (levels of evidence I-V, grades of recommendation A-D). S1 claims are unchanged. Second-source searches (2026-09-24): ERS 2024 was retried through Unpaywall/OpenAlex open copies (University of Birmingham and Erasmus University Pure repositories, Bern BORIS), all bot-challenged and not bypassed; ASCO 2021 (ascopubs PDF) was bot-challenged; Europe PMC searches for an ANZSPM or TSANZ breathlessness guideline or position statement found none. Table rows appended with pmc_text.py --append-tables (2026-09-24); claims from S2 Table 1 (management of conditions contributing to breathlessness) add a 'treat what can be reversed' section. S2 had one table and it was clean.

claims.claim: **Breathlessness is a subjective sense of respiratory discomfort** (air hunger, chest tightness, suffocation), shaped by gas exchange, anxiety and social circumstances such as isolation; anxiety amplifies it.
claims.locator: CareSearch, Flinders University (funded by the Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing), 'Dyspnoea — Clinical Evidence Summary', updated 13 April 2026, https://www.caresearch.com.au/evidence/clinical-evidence-summaries/dyspnoea/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **It is common:** about 70% of people with cancer, particularly thoracic cancer, and 50% to 100% of people with COPD or heart failure.
claims.locator: CareSearch, Flinders University (funded by the Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing), 'Dyspnoea — Clinical Evidence Summary', updated 13 April 2026, https://www.caresearch.com.au/evidence/clinical-evidence-summaries/dyspnoea/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Chronic breathlessness syndrome** (international consensus definition): breathlessness that continues despite the best treatment of its underlying cause and leads to disability. ESMO puts its prevalence in cancer at 20% to 70%, highest in thoracic and advanced cancer and in the final weeks of life.
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology, ESMO Guidelines Committee (Hui D, Maddocks M, Johnson MJ, Ekström M, Simon ST, Ogliari AC, Booth S, Ripamonti CI), ESMO Open 5(6):e001038, doi 10.1136/esmoopen-2020-001038, 'Management of breathlessness in patients with cancer: ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines', published 10 December 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7733213/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Ask the patient to rate it** with the modified Borg scale, a visual analogue scale or the mMRC scale; track change over time.
claims.locator: CareSearch, Flinders University (funded by the Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing), 'Dyspnoea — Clinical Evidence Summary', updated 13 April 2026, https://www.caresearch.com.au/evidence/clinical-evidence-summaries/dyspnoea/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Oxygen saturation and respiratory rate often do not match how breathless the patient feels;** people with advanced cancer can be severely breathless with normal saturation.
claims.locator: CareSearch, Flinders University (funded by the Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing), 'Dyspnoea — Clinical Evidence Summary', updated 13 April 2026, https://www.caresearch.com.au/evidence/clinical-evidence-summaries/dyspnoea/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **In dementia or cognitive impairment, look for non-verbal signs** (agitation, laboured breathing); the Respiratory Distress Observation Scale can help.
claims.locator: CareSearch, Flinders University (funded by the Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing), 'Dyspnoea — Clinical Evidence Summary', updated 13 April 2026, https://www.caresearch.com.au/evidence/clinical-evidence-summaries/dyspnoea/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Screen every patient at each inpatient and outpatient visit (III, B)** with a single-dimension intensity scale of your choice, and ask which activities they have reduced or given up. Patients who avoid exertion often say they are not short of breath, so the symptom goes unseen.
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology, ESMO Guidelines Committee (Hui D, Maddocks M, Johnson MJ, Ekström M, Simon ST, Ogliari AC, Booth S, Ripamonti CI), ESMO Open 5(6):e001038, doi 10.1136/esmoopen-2020-001038, 'Management of breathlessness in patients with cancer: ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines', published 10 December 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7733213/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Look for and treat any reversible condition adding to the breathlessness (II, A)** before or alongside symptom measures; ESMO tabulates the usual contributors and their management.
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology, ESMO Guidelines Committee (Hui D, Maddocks M, Johnson MJ, Ekström M, Simon ST, Ogliari AC, Booth S, Ripamonti CI), ESMO Open 5(6):e001038, doi 10.1136/esmoopen-2020-001038, 'Management of breathlessness in patients with cancer: ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines', published 10 December 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7733213/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Symptomatic anaemia:** consider a transfusion when haemoglobin is below 70–80 g/L, aiming to hold it above that level.
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology, ESMO Guidelines Committee (Hui D, Maddocks M, Johnson MJ, Ekström M, Simon ST, Ogliari AC, Booth S, Ripamonti CI), ESMO Open 5(6):e001038, doi 10.1136/esmoopen-2020-001038, 'Management of breathlessness in patients with cancer: ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines', published 10 December 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7733213/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Malignant pleural effusion:** with under 3 months to live, a simple thoracentesis; with a longer outlook, either an indwelling tunnelled catheter or chemical pleurodesis is reasonable. **Malignant ascites:** paracentesis, with or without a drain left in. **Pericardial effusion or tamponade:** pericardiocentesis, or pericardiectomy with or without a window.
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology, ESMO Guidelines Committee (Hui D, Maddocks M, Johnson MJ, Ekström M, Simon ST, Ogliari AC, Booth S, Ripamonti CI), ESMO Open 5(6):e001038, doi 10.1136/esmoopen-2020-001038, 'Management of breathlessness in patients with cancer: ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines', published 10 December 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7733213/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Central airway obstruction:** endobronchial treatment for a proximal lesion (bronchoscopic debridement, tumour ablation, a stent); radiotherapy for a distal one.
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology, ESMO Guidelines Committee (Hui D, Maddocks M, Johnson MJ, Ekström M, Simon ST, Ogliari AC, Booth S, Ripamonti CI), ESMO Open 5(6):e001038, doi 10.1136/esmoopen-2020-001038, 'Management of breathlessness in patients with cancer: ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines', published 10 December 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7733213/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Lung toxicity from chemotherapy or immunotherapy:** stop the drug and consider a corticosteroid; corticosteroids are also an option for radiation pneumonitis or fibrosis.
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology, ESMO Guidelines Committee (Hui D, Maddocks M, Johnson MJ, Ekström M, Simon ST, Ogliari AC, Booth S, Ripamonti CI), ESMO Open 5(6):e001038, doi 10.1136/esmoopen-2020-001038, 'Management of breathlessness in patients with cancer: ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines', published 10 December 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7733213/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Other contributors:** anticoagulate a pulmonary embolism; give anti-infectives for pneumonia; optimise COPD, asthma or heart failure medically; treat the cause of a metabolic acidosis; for superior vena cava obstruction or lymphangitic spread, treat the cancer, with corticosteroids an anecdotal option; refer cachexia to palliative care, dietetics or physiotherapy.
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology, ESMO Guidelines Committee (Hui D, Maddocks M, Johnson MJ, Ekström M, Simon ST, Ogliari AC, Booth S, Ripamonti CI), ESMO Open 5(6):e001038, doi 10.1136/esmoopen-2020-001038, 'Management of breathlessness in patients with cancer: ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines', published 10 December 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7733213/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **A fan blowing cool air on the face eases air hunger within minutes;** it is cheap, non-invasive and works at home or in hospital.
claims.locator: CareSearch, Flinders University (funded by the Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing), 'Dyspnoea — Clinical Evidence Summary', updated 13 April 2026, https://www.caresearch.com.au/evidence/clinical-evidence-summaries/dyspnoea/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Teach breathing retraining** (pursed-lip and diaphragmatic breathing) and **positioning** (sitting upright or leaning forward).
claims.locator: CareSearch, Flinders University (funded by the Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing), 'Dyspnoea — Clinical Evidence Summary', updated 13 April 2026, https://www.caresearch.com.au/evidence/clinical-evidence-summaries/dyspnoea/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Mindfulness and relaxation may reduce the anxiety that worsens breathlessness;** acupuncture, acupressure and reflexology have emerging, mixed-quality evidence.
claims.locator: CareSearch, Flinders University (funded by the Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing), 'Dyspnoea — Clinical Evidence Summary', updated 13 April 2026, https://www.caresearch.com.au/evidence/clinical-evidence-summaries/dyspnoea/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Graded non-drug measures:** refer to exercise-based rehabilitation, pulmonary or cardiac where lung or heart disease coexists (I, A). Consider a hand-held fan aimed at the face, with or without oxygen; breathing retraining or physiotherapy referral; a trial of a walking aid; and teaching pacing, relieving positions and distraction (each II, B). Offer acupressure or acupuncture if the patient wants it (II, C).
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology, ESMO Guidelines Committee (Hui D, Maddocks M, Johnson MJ, Ekström M, Simon ST, Ogliari AC, Booth S, Ripamonti CI), ESMO Open 5(6):e001038, doi 10.1136/esmoopen-2020-001038, 'Management of breathlessness in patients with cancer: ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines', published 10 December 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7733213/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Opioids, especially morphine, are the mainstay when non-drug measures are not enough;** they lower the brain's perception of breathing discomfort, even with normal oxygen levels.
claims.locator: CareSearch, Flinders University (funded by the Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing), 'Dyspnoea — Clinical Evidence Summary', updated 13 April 2026, https://www.caresearch.com.au/evidence/clinical-evidence-summaries/dyspnoea/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Start morphine low and titrate to response,** watching for sedation and constipation, and reassess the dose regularly because of the risk of respiratory depression.
claims.locator: CareSearch, Flinders University (funded by the Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing), 'Dyspnoea — Clinical Evidence Summary', updated 13 April 2026, https://www.caresearch.com.au/evidence/clinical-evidence-summaries/dyspnoea/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Benzodiazepines (lorazepam, midazolam) are a second-line option when anxiety drives breathlessness;** direct benefit is inconsistent, short-acting agents are preferred, and combining them with opioids risks respiratory depression.
claims.locator: CareSearch, Flinders University (funded by the Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing), 'Dyspnoea — Clinical Evidence Summary', updated 13 April 2026, https://www.caresearch.com.au/evidence/clinical-evidence-summaries/dyspnoea/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Corticosteroids such as dexamethasone help when inflammation or airway oedema contributes,** usually only short term because of immunosuppression, muscle wasting and hyperglycaemia.
claims.locator: CareSearch, Flinders University (funded by the Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing), 'Dyspnoea — Clinical Evidence Summary', updated 13 April 2026, https://www.caresearch.com.au/evidence/clinical-evidence-summaries/dyspnoea/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Oxygen helps hypoxaemic patients but offers little to those with normal oxygen levels;** weigh any comfort against equipment burden, restricted movement and carer load.
claims.locator: CareSearch, Flinders University (funded by the Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing), 'Dyspnoea — Clinical Evidence Summary', updated 13 April 2026, https://www.caresearch.com.au/evidence/clinical-evidence-summaries/dyspnoea/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Morphine dose (S2):** regular low-dose oral morphine is the first-choice drug when severe chronic breathlessness continues despite non-drug measures (II, B). For an opioid-naive patient, start scheduled morphine at 10–30 mg across 24 hours and titrate to symptoms (II, B), for example 5 to 15 mg of extended-release morphine twice a day, lower in renal failure.
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology, ESMO Guidelines Committee (Hui D, Maddocks M, Johnson MJ, Ekström M, Simon ST, Ogliari AC, Booth S, Ripamonti CI), ESMO Open 5(6):e001038, doi 10.1136/esmoopen-2020-001038, 'Management of breathlessness in patients with cancer: ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines', published 10 December 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7733213/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: 🇦🇺 **Australian licence:** the TGA has extended one extended-release oral morphine product (morphine sulfate pentahydrate) to chronic breathlessness at 10–30 mg per 24 hours. Extra immediate-release morphine is not to be given for the breathlessness itself, though coexisting pain may need it.
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology, ESMO Guidelines Committee (Hui D, Maddocks M, Johnson MJ, Ekström M, Simon ST, Ogliari AC, Booth S, Ripamonti CI), ESMO Open 5(6):e001038, doi 10.1136/esmoopen-2020-001038, 'Management of breathlessness in patients with cancer: ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines', published 10 December 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7733213/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Already taking opioids for pain:** consider raising the baseline dose by 25%–50% (V, C). For severe breathlessness on exertion with predictable triggers, a dose taken before the activity may be considered, used sparingly (at most twice daily) and closely monitored, as long-term safety is unknown (II, C).
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology, ESMO Guidelines Committee (Hui D, Maddocks M, Johnson MJ, Ekström M, Simon ST, Ogliari AC, Booth S, Ripamonti CI), ESMO Open 5(6):e001038, doi 10.1136/esmoopen-2020-001038, 'Management of breathlessness in patients with cancer: ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines', published 10 December 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7733213/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **With every opioid start, offer a laxative, plus an antiemetic if needed (I, A);** teach safe opioid use and monitor over time (III, A). ESMO also allows a rescue immediate-release morphine dose of roughly one-sixth of the total daily dose if needed.
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology, ESMO Guidelines Committee (Hui D, Maddocks M, Johnson MJ, Ekström M, Simon ST, Ogliari AC, Booth S, Ripamonti CI), ESMO Open 5(6):e001038, doi 10.1136/esmoopen-2020-001038, 'Management of breathlessness in patients with cancer: ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines', published 10 December 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7733213/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Benzodiazepines are not a first-line drug for breathlessness** because of sedation and delirium (III, D). Use them with caution for breathlessness with anxiety only when opioids have failed (V, C), or for palliative sedation in the last days of life when breathlessness is refractory (IV, C).
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology, ESMO Guidelines Committee (Hui D, Maddocks M, Johnson MJ, Ekström M, Simon ST, Ogliari AC, Booth S, Ripamonti CI), ESMO Open 5(6):e001038, doi 10.1136/esmoopen-2020-001038, 'Management of breathlessness in patients with cancer: ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines', published 10 December 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7733213/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Corticosteroids may be tried when cancer-related breathlessness resists other treatment (II, C).** Do not give palliative oxygen when resting SpO2 is 90% or higher (II, D); if oxygen is trialled, review it within a few days and stop it when the patient notices no benefit. High-flow oxygen (especially in hypoxaemic respiratory failure) and a trial of non-invasive ventilation (especially in hypercapnic failure) may be considered (II, B).
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology, ESMO Guidelines Committee (Hui D, Maddocks M, Johnson MJ, Ekström M, Simon ST, Ogliari AC, Booth S, Ripamonti CI), ESMO Open 5(6):e001038, doi 10.1136/esmoopen-2020-001038, 'Management of breathlessness in patients with cancer: ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines', published 10 December 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7733213/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Not recommended for breathlessness:** sertraline (II, D) and cannabinoids (IV, D); other antidepressants only within clinical trials (V, C).
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology, ESMO Guidelines Committee (Hui D, Maddocks M, Johnson MJ, Ekström M, Simon ST, Ogliari AC, Booth S, Ripamonti CI), ESMO Open 5(6):e001038, doi 10.1136/esmoopen-2020-001038, 'Management of breathlessness in patients with cancer: ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines', published 10 December 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7733213/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Rural and remote patients may wait longer for opioids and oxygen;** CALD patients may decline opioids over addiction worries, so use interpreters and culturally tailored education.
claims.locator: CareSearch, Flinders University (funded by the Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing), 'Dyspnoea — Clinical Evidence Summary', updated 13 April 2026, https://www.caresearch.com.au/evidence/clinical-evidence-summaries/dyspnoea/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander patients:** access can be limited and conventional treatments less acceptable; combining culturally appropriate practices with medical care may improve uptake.
claims.locator: CareSearch, Flinders University (funded by the Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing), 'Dyspnoea — Clinical Evidence Summary', updated 13 April 2026, https://www.caresearch.com.au/evidence/clinical-evidence-summaries/dyspnoea/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Teach carers fan use and repositioning, and support them emotionally;** breathlessness frightens carers and contributes to burnout.
claims.locator: CareSearch, Flinders University (funded by the Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing), 'Dyspnoea — Clinical Evidence Summary', updated 13 April 2026, https://www.caresearch.com.au/evidence/clinical-evidence-summaries/dyspnoea/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Refer to a specialist multimodal breathlessness service where one exists (I, A);** otherwise consider timely referral to palliative care (II, B). Such services usually run 4–6 contacts spread across 4–6 weeks.
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology, ESMO Guidelines Committee (Hui D, Maddocks M, Johnson MJ, Ekström M, Simon ST, Ogliari AC, Booth S, Ripamonti CI), ESMO Open 5(6):e001038, doi 10.1136/esmoopen-2020-001038, 'Management of breathlessness in patients with cancer: ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines', published 10 December 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7733213/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Assess the carer as well:** their psychological state, what information they need and who supports them (III, B); a structured carer needs-assessment tool may help (II, B).
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology, ESMO Guidelines Committee (Hui D, Maddocks M, Johnson MJ, Ekström M, Simon ST, Ogliari AC, Booth S, Ripamonti CI), ESMO Open 5(6):e001038, doi 10.1136/esmoopen-2020-001038, 'Management of breathlessness in patients with cancer: ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines', published 10 December 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7733213/, retrieved 2026-09-24
